tasks.title: Campaign broadcast retry idempotency — no duplicate send / double-count on re-execution
tasks.description: From CAMP-001 review (adversarial #1, HIGH). resolveTargetMembers has no 'already sent' filter, so re-executing a campaign that reverted sending→active (partial failure) re-sends to the whole audience. Eager mode double-SENDS the body (mint short-circuits on the 053 index, but the message already went out) — this is PRE-EXISTING. Claim mode additionally double-COUNTS: sendClaimToMember increments chargeableSentCount + emits the campaign event unconditionally (no per-member guard, since claim mode mints nothing at broadcast). Needs a per-member sent ledger (or use whatsapp_messages when tracking on) to make broadcast at-most-once. Affects billing + WhatsApp duplicate-marketing policy.

tasks.title: Audit quick-reply button payloads vs command-keyword namespace
tasks.description: From CAMP-001 review (adversarial #6). The parser now surfaces template button.payload as message.text, so ALL template quick-reply taps route through matchCommand. An approved template whose quick-reply payload normalizes to a keyword (YES/NO/STOP/HELP/POINTS/REDEEM or CJK equivalents) would trigger that command — e.g. a payload 'STOP' silently unsubscribes the member. CLAIM_<id> is safe. Audit existing approved templates' quick-reply payloads; consider routing button payloads only via explicit prefixes (CLAIM_/REWARD_/JOIN/REDEEM) rather than the bare keyword matcher.

tasks.title: Explicit claim-campaign flag instead of inferring from QUICK_REPLY button shape
tasks.description: From CAMP-001 review (adversarial #4/#5). Broadcast mode is inferred purely from template shape (any QUICK_REPLY button → claim mode, first quick-reply payload overwritten with CLAIM_<id>). An admin picking a template with an unrelated quick-reply ('More info') silently gets claim behavior. A template with BOTH a {{1}} URL button and a quick-reply can't be satisfied in claim mode (no code) → send fails, whole campaign reverts. Add an explicit per-campaign claim flag (schema + builder UI) so mode is intentional, and validate template compatibility at save time.

tasks.title: Claim window cutoff + claim-template body-param validation
tasks.description: From CAMP-001 review (adversarial #9/#11, product decisions). (1) 'completed' campaigns are claimable indefinitely and each tap mints a fresh coupon whose expiry is measured from claim time — decide whether a claim cutoff (campaign end date) is wanted. (2) sendClaimTemplate only supplies customer_name + discount; any other {{param}} in a claim template (e.g. a stray {{code}}) is sent as '' and may be rejected by Meta — validate a claim template's body params are satisfiable in claim mode.

tasks.title: createCampaignCoupon 23505 robustness + null-config mint coverage
tasks.description: From CAMP-001 review (adversarial #2b, QA gap). Migration 053's partial unique index also constrains welcome-flow promo coupons. createCampaignCoupon (coupon-factory.ts) catches unique violations by message.includes('unique') and retries 3x with a NEW code — a 23505 on (campaign_id, member_id) isn't fixed by a new code, so it fails confusingly. Low reachability (welcome mints for fresh member ids), but should reuse isCouponUniqueViolation + treat a (campaign,member) collision as idempotent. Also add a unit test asserting createCampaignBroadcastCoupon's minted-coupon shape for couponConfig:null (no expiry/discount).

tasks.title: Webhook signature verification fails OPEN when secret is unset in production
tasks.description: Found in WH-001 security review (pre-existing): verifySignature returns true when KAPSO_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset — even in production (console.warn 'demo mode' only). If the secret is deleted/renamed/misconfigured, all webhook auth silently disappears: forged inbound messages can spoof any customer phone (JOIN, stamps) for any tenant, since tenant resolves from the unauthenticated payload. Decide: fail closed in production (if (!secret && isProduction) return false) behind an explicit ALLOW_UNSIGNED_WEBHOOKS dev flag, and alert on boot when missing. CAUTION: confirm the current production deployment actually has the secret set before flipping — the demo-mode escape hatch may be load-bearing.

tasks.title: Webhook robustness hardening bundle
tasks.description: Pre-existing items from WH-001 review, none reachable through the WH-001-fixed paths: (1) id-less messages get a crypto.randomUUID() idempotency fallback, so provider redeliveries mint fresh keys and reprocess (double sends) — derive from sha256(rawBody) instead; the x-idempotency-key header fallback is likewise unauthenticated (HMAC covers body only). (2) classifyWebhookKind routes a mixed payload carrying BOTH statuses and messages to status only — inbound silently dropped (fold into WH-003's batch work). (3) Echoes of our own outbound that carry `from` route as normal inbound (auto-reply to ourselves, self service-window) — confirm real Kapso echo shapes via WH-002's raw capture. (4) PhoneNumber.create error message interpolates the raw value; if it ever reaches logs it violates the maskPhone convention — drop the raw value or mask it. (5) A transient Supabase error in resolveRestaurant returns null → 200 'ignored' → legitimate event silently dropped with no retry (repositories swallow errors to null). (6) message.id as JSON object/array with a valid sender: truthy cast passes, PostgREST insert errors non-23505 every attempt → pre-claim 500 storm (pathological payload only). (7) Confirm Kapso's 4xx retry semantics — if it retries any non-2xx like Meta, switch the malformed-JSON 400 to a 200-ignore. (8) route.ts returns handleInbound(...) without await, so its rejections bypass the webhook.error structured log. (9) confirm-marketing-optin emits consent_granted non-transactionally after the flip: if emitEvent throws, the webhook 500s, the Kapso retry finds no pending row and falls through to handleUnknown — customer gets an 'unknown command' reply after a successful YES, event lost (surfaced in REL-001 review as newly-activated behavior).

tasks.title: Webhook observability for ignored events + raw payload capture
tasks.description: Follow-ups from issue #45 review: (1) ignored-event logs carry no message id ('parse returned null' / 'no sender' are anonymous) — thread an id into the parser-null path so production triage can correlate; (2) capture one raw failing payload (only parsed/masked data is logged today) to confirm sender-less events are Kapso status/echo events. Also revisit idempotency-before-processing: a transient routeMessage failure permanently drops the message because the key is claimed first.

tasks.title: Meta webhook parser only reads messages[0] — batch entries dropped

A Meta batch payload with multiple messages silently drops all but the first — and after WH-001, a batch whose first entry lacks a sender drops the real messages behind it. Parse all messages (return an array) or at least the first message WITH a sender.

tasks.title: Scanner visible square misaligned with decode region (iOS portrait)

Needs on-device verification (iOS Safari + Android Chrome).

open_questions.question: consent_records backfill — set existing active members to status='pending' (audit-safe; blocks current campaigns until re-confirmation collected) or status='opted_in' (risky; non-breaking but no proof of consent)?
open_questions.resolution_rationale: User decision: current active member count is small enough that audit-defence risk is bounded. Choose non-breaking option to avoid pausing running campaigns. Backfilled records should be tagged consent_grade='weak' + source='pre-system migration' (per WONB-005) and queued for re-confirmation via WONB-008 once Green quality is established.
open_questions.rationale: Migration writes a consent row per existing member. Wrong choice means a second migration to fix. 'pending' aligns with Meta's audit expectations and the Sales playbook's discovery requirement; 'opted_in' avoids breaking running campaigns but is indefensible if Meta audits.

open_questions.question: Keep all tenants on one shared WABA, or isolate marketing-heavy tenants on a second WABA?
open_questions.resolution_rationale: User decision: each tenant gets their own WABA. Per-tenant scope == per-WABA scope in our architecture. Auto-pause + quality polling + dashboard all operate at tenant level.

open_questions.question: Does Kapso forward Meta account/quality update webhooks, or do we always have to poll?
open_questions.resolution_rationale: User decision: webhook-driven for future performance. Subscribe to Meta account_quality_update webhook (forwarded by Kapso) and persist transitions on receive instead of polling. Mechanism update: WAQ-006 description changes from 'cron job polls Kapso health endpoint every 30 min' to 'webhook handler ingests account_quality_update events'.

open_questions.question: Default per-user marketing cap (1, 2, or 3 marketing templates per 24h)?
open_questions.resolution_rationale: Research: Meta 2026 policy enforces 1 marketing template per business per 24h (resets on user reply). Cross-brand global cap is 2/24h but invisible to us. Going higher routinely triggers 131049 → erodes quality rating. Conservative default protects new tenants; established tenants can raise via tenant_campaign_settings.per_user_marketing_cap. Sources: Meta for Developers per-user-limits doc + Turn.io / Chatarmin / Vonage best-practice writeups.
